_about: Plautus and Terence in English, translator per title. Plautus: Henry T. Riley's prose Comedies (Bohn, 1852; 1913 printing, 2 vols., raw IA, complete) and his Captivi and Mostellaria (clean Gutenberg). Terence: Riley's prose Comedies (Bohn) and George Colman's verse, clean Gutenberg; W. R. Goodluck's Andrian. Paul Nixon's Loeb Plautus vol. 1 (1916; Gutenberg, Latin facing kept) added 2026-10-02 from the bilingual catalogue. Latin-facing Loebs of 1930 or earlier added 2026-10-02 as raw IA OCR (translator per row); the scan's printing was checked for a post-1930 revision notice where its title verso survives.

terence-riley-comedies: The Comedies of Terence, literally translated into English prose
terence-goodluck-andrian: Terence's Andrian, a comedy in five acts
plautus-nixon-v1: Plautus, vol. 1: Amphitryo, Asinaria, Aulularia, Bacchides, Captivi

plautus-riley-comedies-v1: The Comedies of Plautus, vol. 1 (Bohn; 1913 printing)
plautus-riley-comedies-v2: The Comedies of Plautus, vol. 2 (Bohn; 1913 printing)
plautus-nixon-v2: Plautus, vol. 2: Casina, The Casket Comedy, Curculio, Epidicus, Menaechmi (Loeb, 1917)
terence-echard-1733: Terence's Comedies made English, with his life and some remarks at the end, eighth edition, revised by Dr. Echard and Sir R. L'Estrange (London: Knapton and others, MDCCXXXIII)
plautus-evans-trinummus-1883: The Trinummus of T. Maccius Plautus translated into literal English, with notes (London: Simpkin, Marshall, 1883)
terence-cooke-1755-v1: Terence's Comedies, translated into English, together with the original Latin, with critical and explanatory notes, second edition, vol. I (London: R. Ware and others, 1755)
plautus-thornton-1769-v1: Comedies of Plautus, translated into familiar blank verse, second edition revised, vol. I (London: T. Becket and P. A. De Hondt, 1769)
plautus-thornton-1769-v2: Comedies of Plautus, translated into familiar blank verse, second edition revised, vol. II (London: T. Becket and P. A. De Hondt, 1769)
terence-morgan-phormio-1894: The Phormio of Terence, translated into English prose, with a new prologue by J. B. Greenough and the Vatican miniatures (Cambridge, Mass.: C. W. Sever, 1894)

_excluded.Paul Nixon, Loeb Plautus (1916-38): vol. 1 (PG) and vol. 2 (IA) held; vol. 3 (1924) is held back on rights because its only scan is a 1980 reprint (see plautus-nixon-v3's note below); vols. 4-5 first printed 1932 and 1938, not PD
_excluded.Bonnell Thornton's Plautus (1767-74): the first-edition ECCO scans (bim_eighteenth-century_the-comedies-of-plautus-_plautus-titus-maccius_1767_1/_2/_3) read 0.65-0.70, under the bar. The revised second edition's vols. I-II (1769, Google scans, 0.796) are held as plautus-thornton-1769-v1/v2; vols. III-V (1772-74, Warner's continuation) are still wanted. comediesplautus00warngoog reads 0.772, under the bar.
_excluded.comediestranslat02tere: Cooke's Terence (1755), vol. II: no readable title page in the OCR (the preface is signed Thomas Cooke). Not taken under the title-page rule; vol. I is held.

_held.plautus-nixon-v3: held back on rights, not fetched: the only scan (IA plautus03plau) is a 1980 reprint of the 1924 translation carrying a 'Bibliographical Note (1979)', which is not public domain. Converted text would need a per-book cut rule in the converter (not lane B's file) or a clean pre-1931 scan. Was IA plautus03plau: Plautus, vol. 3: The Merchant, The Braggart Warrior, Mostellaria, The Persian (Loeb, 1924)

_translator_unchecked.terence-echard-1733: title page reads 'made English by Mr. Laurence Echard, revised and corrected by Dr. Echard and Sir R. L'Estrange' (eighth edition, MDCCXXXIII); the OCR prints the surname 'EC HARD' and 'Eehard'
